note: Raw SafeContents DER from the PKCS12 authSafe content is decoded into the ASN.1 tree; the bag OIDs later read from it originate here.
Stack buffer oid[128] is declared without initialization; it is reused for the SafeBag bagId OID and then for bag attribute OIDs within the same function, so tail bytes may remain uninitialized.
bagId OID of the current SafeBag is read into oid; a successful read NUL-terminates the string but leaves the tail of the 128-byte stack buffer uninitialized.
The bag OID is dispatched to a bag type by comparing against literal bag OIDs.

The same oid buffer is reused to store the bag attribute OID; when the attribute OID read fails or is too long, oid retains stale/partial content and the following strcmp can read uninitialized tail bytes.
Comparison of the reused oid stack buffer against the literal key-id OID reads bytes beyond what was initialized, producing the use-of-uninitialized-value defect.
